p.src: The story tells how, at that time, Strategist Wu said to Song Gongming, “An opportunity has arisen. A man who came to join us through Shi Yong is also on the closest terms with that scoundrel Luan Tingyu, and is a particularly dear friend of Yang Lin and Deng Fei. He learned that Elder Brother’s attack on the Zhu Family Manor had gone badly, and has offered this stratagem as his means of earning admission to our band. He will arrive shortly. Within five days we can put this plan into effect. What do you think?” When Song Jiang heard this, he was overjoyed and cried, “Excellent!” Only then did his face brighten into a smile.

Now on the coast of Shandong there was a prefecture called Dengzhou. Outside the city of Dengzhou stood a mountain, inhabited by many jackals, wolves, tigers, and leopards that would come forth and maul people. p.src: The two brothers received the deadline writ from the authorities and returned home, where they prepared their concealed bow traps, poisoned arrows, crossbows, iron rakes, and forks. They put on leopard-skin trousers and tiger-skin jackets, then took up their iron forks. They went straight up the mountain in Dengzhou, set their bow traps, and waited in a tree for an entire day. When nothing came of it, they gathered up the traps and descended. The next day they took provisions and went back up to keep watch. As evening drew on, they once more set the traps and climbed into a tree, waiting until the fifth watch, but still there was no sign of anything. They moved the bow traps to the western side of the mountain and set them there, then sat until daybreak, but again caught nothing. Growing anxious, they said, “We must deliver a tiger within three days. If we are late, we shall surely be punished. What are we to do?”

p.src: On the third night, the brothers lay in ambush until the fourth watch and could not help growing weary. They leaned back against each other to sleep, but before their eyes had even closed, they suddenly heard a bow trap snap. They leaped up, seized their steel forks, and looked all around. There they saw a tiger struck by a poisoned arrow, rolling upon the ground. Gripping their steel forks, the brothers advanced. When the tiger saw the men approaching, it fled with the arrow still lodged in it. The brothers gave chase. Before they had gone halfway down the mountain, the poison took full effect. Unable to endure it, the tiger gave a roar and went tumbling head over heels down the slope. Xie Bao said, “Excellent! I know this mountain. The tiger has fallen into the rear garden of Squire Mao’s manor. Let us go down to his house and retrieve it.”

p.src: The brothers took up their steel forks, went straight down the mountain, and knocked at the gate of Squire Mao’s manor. Dawn was only just breaking. The brothers knocked until the manor gate was opened and went inside, and a servant reported their arrival to the squire. After some time, Squire Mao came out. Xie Zhen and Xie Bao set down their steel forks, bowed in greeting, and said, “Uncle, it has been a long time. We have come especially to trouble you today.” Squire Mao said, “My worthy nephews, what brings you here so early? What is it you wish to say?” Xie Zhen replied, “We would not dare disturb your sleep without good cause. The authorities have issued us a writ imposing a deadline under penalty of the cudgel and ordered us to catch a tiger. We waited for three days in succession, and at the fifth watch this morning we finally shot one. Unexpectedly, it rolled down the rear slope into your garden. We beg you to let us pass through and retrieve the tiger.” Squire Mao said, “That is no trouble. Since it fell into my garden, you two should sit for a while. You must be hungry. Eat some breakfast before going to fetch it.” He ordered the servants to prepare breakfast and entertain them. After they had been urged to eat and drink, Xie Zhen and Xie Bao rose and thanked him, saying, “We are deeply grateful for your kindness, Uncle. Please trouble yourself to lead us there and return the tiger to us.” Squire Mao said, “Since it is behind my own manor, what is there to worry about? Sit and have some tea. It will not be too late to fetch it afterward.” Xie Zhen and Xie Bao dared not oppose him and had no choice but to sit down again. A servant brought tea and invited the two men to drink. Squire Mao said, “Now I shall go with my worthy nephews to fetch the tiger.” Xie Zhen and Xie Bao said, “We are deeply grateful, Uncle.”

p.src: Squire Mao led the two men behind the manor and ordered a servant to bring the key and open the gate, but try as they might, it would not open. Squire Mao said, “No one has opened this garden for a long time. The lock must have rusted fast, which is why it will not open. Go fetch an iron hammer and break it open.” A servant brought an iron hammer and smashed the lock open. Everyone entered the garden and searched all along the hillside, but found nothing. Squire Mao said, “My worthy nephews, could you two have seen wrongly and failed to recognize the place clearly? Perhaps it did not fall into my garden after all?” Xie Zhen said, “How could the two of us have seen wrongly? We grew up here—how could we fail to know the place?” Squire Mao said, “Go on searching, then. If you find it, carry it away yourselves.” Xie Bao said, “Brother, come and look. The grass all along here has been rolled flat, and there is a trail of blood over it. How can he say it was not here? Your servants must have carried it away, Uncle.” Squire Mao said, “Do not talk like that. How could the people of my manor have known there was a tiger in the garden, much less carried it away? You yourselves saw us break the lock open before your eyes just now and enter the garden together with you to search. How can you speak this way!” Xie Zhen said, “Uncle, you must return my tiger so that I can deliver it to the authorities.” Squire Mao said, “You two are utterly unreasonable! I kindly invited you to eat and drink, yet you turn around and accuse me of taking your tiger.” Xie Bao said, “What accusation is there in it? Your family holds the office of village headman and received the same official warrant setting a deadline, yet you lacked the ability to catch the beast. Now you have seized the prize we secured and mean to claim the merit for yourselves, leaving us brothers to suffer the deadline beating.” Squire Mao said, “What concern is it of mine if you are beaten?” Xie Zhen and Xie Bao glared and said, “Will you dare let us search the place?” Squire Mao said, “My household, like yours, has its private and public quarters. Just look at these two beggarly fellows, coming here and behaving so insolently!” Xie Bao rushed up before the hall to search, but when he found nothing, anger flared within him and he began smashing things there. Xie Zhen too tore a railing loose before the hall and fought his way inside. Squire Mao shouted, “Xie Zhen and Xie Bao are committing robbery in broad daylight!” After smashing the chairs and tables before the hall, the two saw that everyone in the manor was prepared for them. They promptly dashed out through the gate, pointed back at the manor, and cursed, “You have stolen our tiger. We will settle this with you in court.”

p.src: While the two were still cursing, they saw two or three horsemen approaching the manor at the head of a band of men. Xie Zhen recognized Squire Mao’s son, Mao Zhongyi, and met him with these words: “The servants of your manor took away my tiger. Your father refuses to return it and instead means to beat the two of us.” Mao Zhongyi said, “Those ignorant country louts do not understand their business. They must have deceived my father. Do not be angry, you two. Come home with me, and I will have it returned to you.” Xie Zhen and Xie Bao thanked Mao Zhongyi. He had the manor gate opened and told the two to enter. As soon as Xie Zhen and Xie Bao had entered, he ordered the gate shut and shouted, “Seize them!” Twenty or thirty manor servants rushed out from beneath the two side galleries; together with the men who had followed the horses there just now, they were all constables. The brothers were caught unprepared. Everyone rushed them at once and bound Xie Zhen and Xie Bao. Mao Zhongyi said, “My family shot a tiger ourselves last night. How dare you falsely claim it as yours? You took the opportunity to plunder my family’s property and smashed our household goods. What punishment does that deserve? Delivering you to the prefecture will rid it of a pair of pests as well.” It turned out that during the fifth watch Mao Zhongyi had first delivered the tiger to the prefecture, then brought a number of constables back to arrest Xie Zhen and Xie Bao. The two brothers, failing to grasp the situation, had walked straight into his trap and were given no chance to explain themselves. Squire Mao had the steel forks the two men used brought along with a bundle of supposed stolen goods and many household objects they had smashed. Xie Zhen and Xie Bao were stripped stark naked, their arms pinioned behind them, and escorted to the prefecture. At the prefectural court was a clerk of the Six Offices named Wang Zheng, who was Squire Mao’s son-in-law. He had already gone ahead and reported the matter to the prefect. No sooner had Xie Zhen and Xie Bao been brought before the hall than, without allowing them a word, the men threw them down and beat them, determined to force both to confess that they had falsely claimed the tiger, taken up their steel forks, and used the occasion to plunder property. Unable to endure the torture, Xie Zhen and Xie Bao had no choice but to confess as they were told. The prefect ordered two heavy cangues, each weighing twenty-five catties, placed upon them and had them confined in the main prison. Squire Mao and Mao Zhongyi returned to the manor and conferred: “We cannot let those two wretches live. We had better finish them off entirely and prevent future trouble.” Thereupon father and son went to the prefecture themselves and instructed the clerk Wang Zheng, “Root them out for us once and for all, so no shoot can ever sprout again. We will make the necessary arrangements with the prefect ourselves.”

p.src: Now Yue He was a quick-witted and clever man. He understood every kind of music and could master anything as soon as he began learning it; in any undertaking, he could see the end from the beginning. As for skill with spear and staff, he loved it as dearly as sweets and honey. Seeing that Xie Zhen and Xie Bao were true men of valor, he wished to save them; but a single strand cannot make a cord, nor can one hand clap, so all he could do was bring them a warning. Yue He said, “You two should know that Guard Bao has now taken money from Squire Mao and will certainly seek your lives. What are you going to do?” Xie Zhen replied, “Had you not mentioned Commander Sun, that would have been the end of it. But since you have spoken of him, we beg you to carry a message for us.” Yue He asked, “To whom would you have me carry it?” Xie Zhen said, “I have an elder sister on my father’s side who is married to Commander Sun’s younger brother. She now lives at Ten-Li Post outside the eastern gate. She is my paternal aunt’s daughter and is called Gu Dasao, the ‘Tigress.’ She keeps an inn, and at home they also slaughter cattle and run gambling games. Twenty or thirty men together could not get near my sister, and even her husband Sun Xin, for all his skill, is no match for her. Of all people, that sister alone is closest to the two of us. The paternal aunt of Sun Xin and Sun Li was our mother, so the two of them are also our maternal cousins. Please secretly send word to her and tell her what has happened to me. My sister will surely come herself to save us.”

He fears your two brothers may be released, so he will never let the matter rest. He is certain to do them in, and at this rate they will surely die at his hands. Unless we break into the jail, there is no other way to save them.” Gu Dasao said, “Then you and I will go tonight.” Sun Xin laughed. “How rash you are! You and I must devise a sound long-term plan. Once we have broken them out, we will also need somewhere to go. Without my elder brother and these other two men, we cannot carry this off.” Gu Dasao asked, “Who are these two?” Sun Xin said, “They are Zou Yuan and Zou Run, the gambling-loving uncle and nephew. They are now in Tai Valley on Mount Dengyun, where they have gathered a band and live by robbery. They are very close friends of mine. If we gain their aid, the affair will succeed.” Gu Dasao said, “Mount Dengyun is not far from here. Go through the night and invite the uncle and nephew here to discuss the matter.” Sun Xin said, “I will go at once. Prepare wine, food, and dishes. Please come inside, Brother, and we shall talk.” Sun Li went inside. Sun Xin instructed the servants to take the soldiers who had accompanied the horses to drink at the tavern opposite. He then had a servant lead the horse away and invited Sun Li into the inner rooms to sit. After a long while, Sun Xin said, “Brother, please take Sister-in-law into the bedroom to see the patient.” Sun Li entered the bedroom with Madam Yue, but saw no patient there. Sun Li asked, “In which room is your wife lying ill?” Just then Gu Dasao came in from outside, with Zou Yuan and Zou Run behind her. Sun Li said, “Sister-in-law, what illness is it that you truly have?” Gu Dasao said, “My respects to you, Elder Brother. I am suffering from an illness that can only be cured by rescuing my brothers.” Sun Li said, “How very strange! What brothers are you rescuing?” Gu Dasao said, “Elder Brother, do not pretend to be deaf and dumb. You are in the city; surely you know those two are my brothers—and are they not your brothers as well?” Sun Li said, “I know nothing of the circumstances. Which two brothers do you mean?” Gu Dasao said, “With all respect, Elder Brother, matters are urgent today, so I must speak plainly: Xie Zhen and Xie Bao were entrapped by Squire Mao of Mount Dengyun in league with Clerk Wang, and their lives may be taken at any moment. These two heroes and I have settled our plans: we shall storm the city prison, rescue my two brothers, and all join the band at Liangshan Marsh. Since the affair may come to light tomorrow, we feared you would be implicated first. That is why I feigned illness and invited you and Sister-in-law here, so that we might discuss the matter fully. If you refuse to go with us, we shall depart for Liangshan Marsh by ourselves. What justice is there in the imperial court nowadays? Those who flee suffer nothing, while those who remain are prosecuted. As the saying goes, ‘The one nearest the fire is scorched first.’ You would be prosecuted and imprisoned in our stead, and then there would be no one even to bring you food or rescue you. What do you think, Elder Brother?” Sun Li said, “But I am an officer of Dengzhou! How could I dare do such a thing?” Gu Dasao said, “Since you refuse, today we shall first fight you to the death.” Gu Dasao instantly drew two knives from her person, while Zou Yuan and Zou Run each pulled out a dagger. Sun Li cried, “Wait, Sister-in-law! Do not be so hasty! Let me consider the matter carefully, and we shall discuss it at leisure.” Madam Yue was so terrified that for a long while she could not utter a word. Gu Dasao continued, “If you will not go, we shall send Sister-in-law on her way first, then carry out the deed ourselves.” Sun Li said, “Even if we are to proceed, you must let me return home to pack our belongings and investigate the true situation before we act.” Gu Dasao said, “Elder Brother, your brother-in-law Yue has already passed us the information. We can storm the prison on the one hand and fetch the baggage on the other; it will not be too late.” Sun Li sighed and said, “Since all of you have resolved to do this, how can I refuse? Otherwise, am I to face prosecution for you afterward? Very well, very well, very well! Let us all plan it together and then act.” They first told Zou Yuan to return to the stronghold on Mount Dengyun, gather the wealth, men, and horses, and bring twenty trusted followers to assemble at the tavern. Zou Yuan departed. They also sent Sun Xin into the city to seek news from Yue He. Having fixed the time with him, they secretly conveyed the plan to Xie Zhen and Xie Bao. Sun Xin also had seven or eight wholly trusted servants at home, and together with the dozen or more soldiers Sun Li had brought, they numbered over forty men in all.

p.src: Now, in the Dengzhou prefectural prison, Warden Bao had accepted Squire Mao’s money and gifts and sought only to take the lives of Xie Zhen and Xie Bao. That day, Yue He stood just inside the prison gate by the lion’s-mouth entrance, holding his fire-and-water staff, when he heard the pull-bell ring. “Who is it?” he called. Gu Dasao answered, “A woman bringing food.” Yue He had already looked through the peephole. He came and opened the gate, let Gu Dasao in, and shut it again. As he led her beneath the corridor, Warden Bao, who was in the central pavilion, saw them and shouted, “Who is this woman? How dare she enter the prison to deliver food? Since ancient times, no outside breath has been admitted into a prison.” Yue He said, “She is the elder sister of Xie Zhen and Xie Bao, and has come to bring them food.” Warden Bao shouted, “Do not let her enter! Take the food from her and carry it in yourselves.” Yue He took the food, then opened the cell door and handed it to the two prisoners. Xie Zhen and Xie Bao asked, “Uncle, what has become of the matter you spoke of last night?” Yue He said, “Your sister has come in. We need only wait for those inside and outside to act together.” Yue He then unlocked the cangue-bench for the two of them. Just then a young jailer came in and reported, “Commandant Sun is knocking at the gate and insists on entering.” Warden Bao said, “He is a garrison officer. What business has he in my prison? Do not open the gate!” Gu Dasao edged step by step toward the central pavilion. Another cry came from outside: “Commandant Sun has lost patience and is pounding on the gate!” Warden Bao grew angry and came down from the pavilion. Gu Dasao gave a great shout: “Where are my brothers?” She instantly drew two gleaming sharp knives from her clothes. Seeing that something was amiss, Warden Bao ran toward the outside of the pavilion. Xie Zhen and Xie Bao lifted their cangues, squeezed out through the cell opening, and came face-to-face with Warden Bao. Caught unprepared, Warden Bao was struck hard by the end of Xie Bao’s cangue, which smashed his skull to pieces. At once Gu Dasao struck, stabbing down three or five young jailers. They all raised a battle cry and fought their way out of the prison. Sun Li and Sun Xin held off two men at the entrance. When they saw the four emerge from the prison, they all ran together toward the prefectural offices. Zou Yuan and Zou Run had already emerged from the prefectural offices carrying Clerk Wang’s head. People in the streets raised a great clamor, while the band rushed out of the city first. Commandant Sun rode at the rear, bow bent and arrow nocked. Every household along the street shut its doors, and no one dared come out. The prefectural constables recognized Commandant Sun, and none dared step forward to block him. The whole company clustered around Sun Li and rushed through the city gate. They went straight to the Ten-Li Marker and helped Madam Yue into the cart. Gu Dasao mounted a horse and rode alongside the cart. Xie Zhen and Xie Bao said to the others, “That accursed old thief Squire Mao is our mortal enemy. How can we leave without taking revenge?” Sun Li said, “You are right.” He ordered his brother Sun Xin and his brother-in-law Yue He to escort the cart onward first, saying, “We shall catch up afterward.” Sun Xin and Yue He escorted the cart and departed ahead of the others.

p.src: Within a day or two they reached Shi Yong's tavern. Zou Yuan greeted him and asked about Yang Lin and Deng Fei. Shi Yong replied by telling them how Song Gongming had gone to attack Zhu Family Manor and how both men had accompanied him. The attackers had been defeated twice, and reports said that Yang Lin and Deng Fei had both been trapped there; what had become of them was unknown. They heard in full how the three sons of Zhu Family Manor were all valiant men and had the further aid of their martial instructor, Luan Tingyu the “Iron Cudgel”; this was why two assaults had failed to break the manor. When Sun Li had heard it all, he laughed loudly. “We have come to join the great stronghold, but as yet have not the least achievement to our names. What if I offer a stratagem to capture Zhu Family Manor, as the service by which we earn admission?” Shi Yong was delighted. “I should like to hear this excellent plan.” Sun Li said, “That fellow Luan Tingyu and I learned our martial arts from the same master. He knows the spear and saber methods I learned, and I know all the skills that he learned. Today we need only pretend that I have been transferred from Dengzhou to take up a guard post in Yunzhou and have stopped here on my way to pay him a visit. He will certainly come out to welcome us. Once we have gained admission, we shall work from within while you attack from without, and the great undertaking is certain to succeed. What do you think of this plan?” Before he had finished discussing the plan with Shi Yong, a junior officer came to report: “Scholar Wu has come down from the mountain and is on his way to aid the force at Zhu Family Manor.” On hearing this, Shi Yong immediately told the soldier to hurry and inform the strategist, asking him to come there for a meeting. Before he had finished speaking, troops and horses had already arrived before the tavern. They were Lü Fang, Guo Sheng, and the three Ruan brothers; behind them came the strategist Wu Yong at the head of five hundred men and horses. Shi Yong welcomed them into the tavern and introduced the entire party. He then related in detail how they wished to join the band and had offered a stratagem. Wu Yong was overjoyed when he heard this. “Since you worthy heroes are willing to help our stronghold succeed, do not go up the mountain just yet. May I trouble you to proceed to Zhu Family Manor and carry out this undertaking, thereby completing this meritorious service?” Sun Li and all the others were delighted and agreed with one voice. Wu Yong said, “I shall set out now. When the armies meet as arranged, our troops will advance first, and you worthy heroes are to follow after us and come on together.”

p.src: When Scholar Wu had finished making his arrangements, he went first to Song Jiang's camp. Finding Song Gongming with knitted brows and anxiety upon his face, Wu Yong had wine served to dispel his gloom. He explained in full how Shi Yong, Yang Lin, and Deng Fei had all previously known a certain man: Sun Li, the Dengzhou garrison commandant known as the “Sick Yuchi,” who had learned from the same martial master as Luan Tingyu, the instructor at Zhu Family Manor. Eight of them had now come together to seek refuge in the great stronghold and join the band, and had specially offered this stratagem as their service of admission. Their plan had now been settled: they would act in this manner, coordinating the attack from within and without, and afterward would come to pay their respects to their elder brother. When Song Jiang heard this, he was overjoyed. All his gloom vanished beyond the highest clouds, and he quickly ordered wine and a banquet prepared within the camp to await and entertain them. Now Sun Li ordered his own attendants and the others to remain with the carts, followers, and horses and camp together. Taking only Xie Zhen, Xie Bao, Zou Yuan, Zou Run, Sun Xin, Mistress Gu, and Yue He—eight persons in all including himself—he went to pay his respects to Song Jiang, and all the proper courtesies were exchanged. Song Jiang served them wine and laid a feast for their entertainment; there is no need to dwell upon it. Scholar Wu secretly passed orders to the leaders, instructing them what to do on the third day and what to do on the fifth. When the instructions were complete, Sun Li and the others received the plan and set out with the carts, attendants, and horses for Zhu Family Manor, there to gain admission and carry out the scheme. Scholar Wu then said, “I must trouble Warden Dai to make a journey back to the stronghold. Quickly fetch these four chieftains for me; I have a use for them elsewhere.” Indeed, when Dai Zong raced through the night to bring those four men, the outcome would be that new wings were added to the heroes of the marsh, while at the manor not a trace of its former lords remained. But as for which four men Scholar Wu summoned, listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
